section_summary.extract_value: The section reports two hierarchical moderated regression models testing BMI, three body size discrepancy measures (current-personal ideal, current-ethnic group ideal, current-typical ethnic female peer), and their interactions as predictors of two positive body image outcomes (body appreciation and body image flexibility). Regression results indicate BMI was the strongest predictor for both outcomes, the personal-ideal discrepancy contributed unique variance to both (and to body image flexibility more strongly), and none of the BMI-by-discrepancy interactions were significant. The text describes model fit (e.g., ~22% variance explained for body appreciation; ~34% for body image flexibility) but provides no sample, demographic, instrument names (BAS/BAS-2), correlation coefficients, or procedural details about BMI measurement.

section_summary.extract_value: This section reports two hierarchical moderated regression models conducted on a single sample (N = 223) testing BMI and three body size discrepancy scores as predictors of body appreciation and body image flexibility.
